concepts.def: Across medieval Europe, land was held in exchange for service and loyalty, binding lords, vassals and peasants in a hierarchy of obligation.
The manor was the basic economic unit: peasants worked the lord's land and their own strips, owing labour services and dues, with serfs tied to the estate.
Trade revival after about 1000 swelled towns, where merchant and craft guilds regulated quality, prices and the training of apprentices and journeymen.
Long-distance routes such as the Silk Roads, the Hanseatic League in northern Europe and Italian Mediterranean shipping linked Europe, the Islamic world and Asia.
Religious institutions structured daily life: the Church dominated education and charity in Europe, while madrasas and waqf endowments served similar roles in the Islamic world.
Plague spread west along trade routes, killing perhaps a third or more of Europe's population and transforming wages, labour and landholding.

mcqs.q: In the feudal system, what did a vassal typically receive in return for service?
options: A fief - land granted by a lord
A guild membership
A cash salary paid by the king's bank
A seat in an elected parliament
An association of artisans in one trade that regulated training, quality and prices
A tax collected by the Church
A band of travelling knights
A royal court of law

mcqs.q: How did the Black Death affect labour in Western Europe?
options: Labour shortages pushed wages up and helped weaken serfdom
Wages collapsed because there were too many workers
It had no measurable economic effects
It permanently ended all trade with Asia
Overland and sea routes linking China, Central Asia, the Middle East and Europe, carrying goods and ideas
Roman military roads across Gaul
Pilgrimage routes to Jerusalem only
Canals built across Persia

mcqs.q: Were medieval serfs the same as slaves?
options: Serfs were slaves with no rights of any kind.
Serfs were paid professional soldiers of the lord.
No - serfs were unfree and tied to the land, but they held customary rights, worked their own plots, and were not generally bought and sold as individual property.
The Black Death was confined to the British Isles.

mcqs.q: Was the medieval economy static and unchanging?
options: No - between about 1000 and 1300 population grew strongly, new towns were founded, field rotation improved, and trade fairs and banking expanded.
Nothing changed economically during the so-called Dark Ages.
Medieval Europe had no money and used only barter.
Serfs were paid professional soldiers of the lord.

mcqs.q: Did the Black Death affect only Europe?
options: No - the pandemic spread along trade routes across Asia, the Middle East and North Africa, devastating cities such as Cairo as well as European ones.
The Black Death was confined to the British Isles.
Serfs were paid professional soldiers of the lord.
The plague of the fourteenth century was a purely European event.
